Nxeon hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`). Admin panel has an existing "Dedicated IP pool" page (Infrastructure → IP pool) backed by the `DedicatedIp` Prisma model (`prisma/schema.prisma`) and `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`'s `syncDedicatedIpPool()`/`allocateDedicatedIp()`/`releaseDedicatedIp()`. Today it shows one flat table: IP address / status / assigned-to (Server hostname) / virtual MAC / reverse DNS, with summary cards (Total IPs, Assigned, OVH cost, IP revenue).

## The ask

The owner wants a distinct section in this page for IPs that power **Nxeon's own internal infrastructure** (hosting nodes, the cold-email relay, etc.) — separate from IPs assigned to real customer servers. Right now the page has no way to tell them apart; an internal-infra IP either shows a stale/wrong "assigned to" (a real bug fixed earlier today — see below) or shows blank, indistinguishable from something actually broken.

## Ground truth — the real purpose of every IP currently in the pool (verified today, use directly, don't re-derive)

| Address | Real purpose | Category |
|---|---|---|
| `51.79.154.233` | Customer VPS `primegc1` (real signup) | Customer |
| `51.79.168.98` | Cold-email relay, Proxmox VM 9010 (`coldemail-relay`) — **not tracked via any `Server` row at all**, it's platform infrastructure provisioned directly via the OVH API outside the normal customer flow | Internal — "Cold Email Relay" |
| `51.79.181.111` | Customer game server `terraria-i2ydef` (real signup) | Customer |
| `51.79.226.200` | VM 105 `studionexis-soul` — owned by `User.email = nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com`, the platform operator's own internal account (not a customer signup) | Internal — "Owner-operated site (StudioNexis/Soul Pilates)" |
| `51.79.226.201` | The shared-hosting node, Proxmox VM 200 (`hosting-1`) — reaches this IP entirely through a live iptables DNAT rule (`-d 51.79.226.201/32 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.20.0.200`), has NO OVH Virtual MAC bound at all, and its `DedicatedIp` row currently has `serverId: null` (correctly — it was never meant to link to a `Server` row) | Internal — "Shared Hosting Node" |
| `51.79.226.215` | VM 106 `nexis-app` — same owner account as `studionexis-soul` above | Internal — "Owner-operated site (Nexis app)" |

(`51.79.162.96` is the dedicated server's own primary IP, excluded from this pool entirely by existing code — leave that exclusion as-is. A 7th IP, `51.161.106.125`, is a recently-ordered but wrong-datacenter-zone IP currently being cancelled/swapped via OVH support — don't hardcode anything about it, it may not exist in the account by the time this ships.)

## What to build

1. **Schema**: add a way to mark a `DedicatedIp` row as internal-use with a human label — e.g. `purpose: DedicatedIpPurpose @default(CUSTOMER)` (enum: `CUSTOMER`, `INTERNAL`) plus `purposeLabel: String?` (free text, e.g. "Cold Email Relay", "Shared Hosting Node") for INTERNAL rows. Check how schema changes get applied in this repo (no `prisma/migrations/` history — `npx prisma db push` is the established convention here) and follow it; also write the raw SQL to a `prisma/manual-migration-*.sql` file matching the existing convention (check `prisma/manual-migration-critical-email-retry.sql` from earlier work today for the exact format/style to match).
2. **Seed the 3 known internal rows** with a one-off script/migration data update: `51.79.168.98` → INTERNAL / "Cold Email Relay", `51.79.226.201` → INTERNAL / "Shared Hosting Node", `51.79.226.200` → INTERNAL / "Owner-operated site (StudioNexis/Soul Pilates)", `51.79.226.215` → INTERNAL / "Owner-operated site (Nexis app)". Leave `51.79.154.233` and `51.79.181.111` as CUSTOMER (the default).
3. **`syncDedicatedIpPool()`** (`lib/dedicated-ip.ts`): when it imports a genuinely NEW IP, default `purpose: "CUSTOMER"` — this function's job is populating the pool customers draw from, it should never need to know about internal-use IPs (those get marked by hand, as above, since they're rare one-off infrastructure allocations, not something the sync should try to auto-detect).
4. **Admin UI** (find the actual page — likely under `app/admin/infrastructure/` or similar, check `lib/admin-groups.ts`'s `fleet` group for the "IP pool" tab's href to find the right file): split the table into two sections — "Nxeon Services" (the INTERNAL rows, each showing its `purposeLabel` instead of a customer hostname) above or below "Customer-assigned" (the CUSTOMER rows, unchanged from today). Keep the existing summary cards working correctly (Total IPs, Assigned, OVH cost should still sum across both categories — IP revenue should presumably only apply to CUSTOMER rows if it's computing revenue-per-IP, check the existing calculation and adjust only if it's now double-counting or miscounting because of the new category, otherwise leave it).
5. If there's an existing admin action to edit/manage a `DedicatedIp` row, add the ability to set/change `purpose`/`purposeLabel` from the UI too (a small form or inline edit) so a future internal allocation doesn't need a raw SQL update — check for an existing `lib/actions-*.ts` file backing this page and extend it following its existing conventions, rather than inventing a new pattern.

## Ground rules

- `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-ippool -b feature/ip-pool-internal-category`, symlink `node_modules`/`.env`, work only there. Give the worktree its OWN real `node_modules` (via `npm ci`, not just a symlink) before running `npx prisma generate` or anything schema-related — a symlinked `node_modules` caused a real incident earlier today where a schema change briefly overwrote production's generated Prisma client. This is a hard requirement, not optional.
- `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass clean.
- This touches a schema change and the admin IP-management page — moderate risk. Commit your work but do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging/production, do NOT run `prisma db push` against any live database. Stop after committing and report back for review.
- If Playwright or similar is available and you can get an authenticated admin session (check for precedent from other agents today), screenshot the updated IP pool page. If not, clean build + code review is the fallback — say clearly which you did.

Report back: what you built, the schema diff / migration SQL, the commit hash, a screenshot if you got one, and what manual steps remain (e.g. "review, then `db push` on staging, deploy, verify the seeded categories render correctly, then production").
